First Jobs to GO #AI

Customer service representative, tier 1.
🎧 Salesforce cut about 4,000 support roles after ticket volume fell. In announcements that name AI, customer support is the most-replaced job — roughly 71,500 seats at 14 companies since 2024. The seat that goes is the rep on password resets, order status, and refund policy. The rep on a cancellation threat stays. The Bureau of Labor Statistics has customer service representatives on a −5.5% path through 2034, off a base of 2.8 million.

Data entry keyer. ⌨️ 
About 142,000 people in the U.S. still hold this title, median pay around $43,000. The BLS outlook is −26% by 2034, the steepest on the clerical list. Keying invoices, applications, and form fields into a database is a solved task. The title does not get a successor. It gets absorbed by the system that used to receive the file.

Telemarketer. 
📞 About 67,000 telemarketers, outlook −22% through 2034. A voice tool can hold the script, the lead list, and the disposition code. An account executive is a different job. A dialer reading a fixed pitch is not.

Bookkeeping clerk, payroll clerk, and executive secretary. 
📒 The World Economic Forum puts data-entry clerks, executive secretaries, and accounting, bookkeeping, and payroll clerks at more than half of the job destruction employers expect, with 25–35% less demand for those seats. 

Legal secretary and junior paralegal on first-pass review. 
📄 Scan, extract, compare, flag. A 2026 ranking of 756 jobs put telephone operators at 83% exposure and legal secretaries and administrative assistants at 64%. Contract translators on standard commercial text are already in a draft-and-check workflow. Court interpreters and litigators are not.

Junior copywriter and production graphic designer. 
✍️ Product blurbs, ad variants, and first-pass layout. One 2026 tracker put junior copywriter hiring down about 25% and entry graphic design down about 19%. The campaign lead stays.

#Hiring 🚀
The seats above are getting pulled. These are the ones funded teams are filling.
Prestigious Series A–D startups. Top VC-backed. U.S. Physical presence in the U.S. or Canada required.

What they keep asking for: 
Founding engineers and product engineers who have shipped from 0 to 1. Builders with 2–5 years who have owned a surface end to end. 
Operators who have already built inside Series A–D companies. 
Researchers from top 30 CS schools in the U.S. and worldwide.

🛂 Visa transfers are open for many of these roles. Brand-new sponsorships are rare.

Fourteen applicants from Eleuthera.

Hire three, and the standard hiring-bias test says the system is fair. Hire two, and it flags discrimination. Hire four, and Eleuthera suddenly looks favoured.

One hiring decision, three verdicts. That is the needle swinging in the picture.

The four-fifths rule sits behind most AI hiring audits, including the ones New York City now requires. It was built for large applicant pools. New York's rules even let auditors leave out categories under 2 per cent of the data. Measured by population, 15 of our 19 islands fall under that line.

Any small island state that buys hiring software from abroad inherits the same problem, plus a model trained on other people's names, schools and addresses.

The fixes need no new legislation: pool results across hiring cycles, use exact tests, map local proxies like surname and secondary school, and get audit rights into the vendor contract before you sign.

For Bahamian employers: section 50 of the Data Protection Act, 2025, on solely automated decisions, is not in force yet. Document your human review step before it is.

The full piece has the charts and the arithmetic. Please check my numbers.
Has anyone seen a hiring-bias audit built for a small island population? I have not, and I would like to.

That is not a claim about what the March should have done. It is a measure of what time and sustained organization can do together.

They are scheduled to meet with leaders in technology, public service, and entrepreneurship about AI governance, the future of work, and health equity.

But on November 7, what happens to all that talent, influence, access, and possibility?What if AfroTech 2027 began on November 7, 2026?

Keep the connections working throughout the year. 

Track training, hiring, business contracts, investment, and city-level pilots at 30, 90, and 365 days.

Then make the November 2027 conference a report card as well as a celebration.

The mayors’ participation could be the start of something much larger than a roundtable. 

Thirteen cities could help test what a year-round Black technology and economic network can actually deliver.

We already know how to fill the room.

Can we build a system that keeps working when the room is empty?

AI should not have one permission level across the entire business.

A system that categorizes an email should not have the same authority as one that approves a refund, changes a contract, or moves money.

A practical AI workflow needs three permission levels:

1. Automate

Use full automation when the task is low-risk, reversible, and easy to verify.

Examples:

• Classifying incoming requests
• Routing support tickets
• Extracting data from standard documents
• Creating internal summaries
• Sending routine status notifications

2. Assist + approve

AI prepares the action, but a person reviews and approves it when the outcome could affect a customer, a financial record, or an operational commitment.

Examples:

• Drafting customer responses
• Recommending refunds or discounts
• Updating important records
• Producing management reports
• Suggesting changes to schedules or inventory

3. Human decides

Keep the final decision with a qualified person when the action is high-risk, sensitive, difficult to reverse, or legally significant.

Examples:

• Hiring or termination decisions
• Credit or eligibility decisions
• Contract approval
• Large financial transactions
• Legal, medical, or safety-related decisions

The important question is not only:

“Can AI perform this task?”

It is also:

“What authority should AI have, and when must it escalate?”

Good AI automation includes a clear escalation path before the first workflow goes live.

لا يجب أن يمتلك الذكاء الاصطناعي مستوى صلاحية واحداً في جميع عمليات الشركة.

فالنظام الذي يصنّف رسالة بريد إلكتروني لا يجب أن يمتلك الصلاحية نفسها التي يمتلكها نظام يوافق على استرداد مبلغ، أو يعدّل عقداً، أو ينقل أموالاً.

يحتاج سير العمل العملي للذكاء الاصطناعي إلى ثلاثة مستويات من الصلاحيات:

1. أتمتة كاملة

تُستخدم عندما تكون المهمة منخفضة المخاطر، ويمكن التراجع عنها، ويسهل التحقق من نتيجتها.

أمثلة:

• تصنيف الطلبات الواردة
• توجيه تذاكر الدعم
• استخراج البيانات من المستندات القياسية
• إعداد الملخصات الداخلية
• إرسال إشعارات الحالة الروتينية

2. مساعدة مع موافقة بشرية

يقترح الذكاء الاصطناعي الإجراء، لكن يقوم شخص بمراجعته والموافقة عليه عندما تؤثر النتيجة في العميل أو السجلات المالية أو الالتزامات التشغيلية.

أمثلة:

• صياغة ردود العملاء
• اقتراح مبالغ الاسترداد أو الخصومات

• إعداد التقارير الإدارية
• اقتراح تغييرات على الجداول أو المخزون

3. القرار النهائي للإنسان

يبقى القرار النهائي بيد شخص مؤهل عندما يكون الإجراء عالي المخاطر أو حساساً أو يصعب التراجع عنه أو له أثر قانوني.

السؤال المهم ليس فقط:

«هل يستطيع الذكاء الاصطناعي تنفيذ المهمة؟»

بل أيضاً:

«ما الصلاحية التي يجب أن يمتلكها، ومتى يجب تصعيد القرار للإنسان؟»

الأتمتة الجيدة تبدأ بتصميم مسار تصعيد واضح قبل تشغيل أول سير عمل.

The Philippines just gave AI sales teams a better ROI pitch.
And it has nothing to do with firing people.

The country's IT-BPM industry expects revenue to grow about 6.4% next year.

Headcount?
Only about 2.6%.

Jack Madrid from IBPAP put it plainly: revenue is starting to grow faster than headcount as AI gets used across the industry.

That is a much better sales story for Southeast Asia than:
“Our AI replaces 3 employees.”

Especially when that beautiful ROI calculator was built using US salaries.

Cebu Pacific is a good example.

After rolling out enterprise AI:

Contract review:
2.5 hours → 1.2 hours

Project intake:
5 days → 1 day

Engineering search:
10–15 minutes → under 10 seconds

Notice what is interesting here.
The value is showing up in how much work the same team can get through.

That gives me a very different question for a buyer in Manila, Jakarta or HCMC:
“If your team handles 100 cases today, could they handle 140 next year without hiring 40% more people?”

Now we have something a CFO can actually argue about.

Because “we saved 3,000 hours” sounds fantastic...

until everyone is still employed, the backlog is still there and Finance asks where exactly the money went 

This is where I think many US AI companies will struggle in SEA.

They bring an ROI sheet built around expensive American labour.

Change USD to PHP or IDR.
Change the customer logo.
Done. “Localised.”

I would rebuild the business case around:
- more work per team  
- fewer future hires  
- shorter queues  
- faster revenue  
- less rework

Few thoughts on Inc42 Media #CTOSummit2026 after digesting it for a few days:

•  "Platform is the moat", declared Prabhu Ram from Razorpay, who also had the most remarkable presentation of the day that was saved for the last. 

    This similar theme was also etched out by Porter Stansberry on X: https://lnkd.in/gETBFcke where he talks about certain platforms essentially being computing toll booths that bring switching cost along with it. Focus on building such a platform, the rest will follow.

• Given the dynamic nature of the current landscape, signing of multi-year contracts might become a thing of the past, as the focus shifts to outcome or consumption-based meter pricing. Adding intelligence on top of the platform has only made the moat of the platform deeper, increasing the overall switching cost. 

• Autonomous AI agents as deployed at Razorpay (called "Slash") have been great at fixing bugs. The job of developers is to ensure working guardrails and evals around those PR's. Besides security, guardrails and evals were the second-most mentioned terms throughout the event, if am not wrong.

• Open-weight models are the future for coding-related tasks. I believe Razorpay mentioned only 7% workload using frontier models.

• Razorpay, Rapido and Zomato (Nugget) really showed up with their demo's. Talking about their shift to a knowledge AI platform, similar to Stripe. 

• AI hasn't necessarily caused job loss as was predicted. Instead, with increased productivity, businesses are expanding to other verticals. "Rising tide lifts all boats" at play.  However, there were concerns raised on hiring and one specifically mentioning vibe coded projects by graduates don't count.

• Developers need to be system thinkers but then someone mentioned AI is the architect and we are just reviewers. I guess everybody is grappling with the right analogy for the changing times 😅. Good judgement remains key regardless.

• With regards to education, there was no neat consensus on the direction a student should take for better prospects. Mathematics, Humanities were mentioned. Somebody in the audience pointed out fundamentals still matter. 

• Free drinks, ftw! Being a foodie, I would have loved to just find a place to sit and chow on all the delicious food in offering.. but the occasion called for talking and chewing at the same time.

Overall, a highly edifying experience set on a great venue. A bit schmexpensive for my liking, however you could get free passes if you are part of an invited cohort.
